messages:
tess (support): FYI incoming from Venue: they've been seeing sustained 429s this morning for their dedicated pool. They say TPS spiked and then the pool started rejecting. Customer report: token-per-second SLO violations and 'burst credits exhausted'. Can we triage?

venue-sre: Confirming. Started at 08:12 UTC — sudden jump to ~1.8k TPS, was fine earlier. We're on a 4-GPU reserved pool (pool-id: pool-vn-14). Logs show admission controller started returning 429s ~08:15.

ops-bot: [alert] DedicatedPool(pool-vn-14) admission_reject > 1000 req/min since 08:15 UTC. BurstCredits remaining: 0. Autoscale events: scale_up_requested at 08:18, scale_up_failed: quota-exceeded.

ajay (oncall): Can someone paste the exact 429 response body and the admission controller debug log around 08:14-08:20? Also need recent config for admission headroom thresholds.

venue-sre: 429 payload snippet: `{ "error": "admission_rejected", "reason": "burst_credits_exhausted", "details": { "credits": 0, "window_secs": 60 } }`

venue-sre: admission debug lines: `admission: request=abcd node_pool=pool-vn-14 current_tps=1800 headroom=100 allowed=100 rejected=1700` then `admission: burst_credits=0 -> rejecting`.

simon (infra): Looking at metrics — pool CPU/GPU utilization jumped to ~95% by 08:14. Autoscaler attempted to add 2 nodes at 08:18 but failed with cloud quota error (VM quota) so no extra capacity came up. Headroom policy is set to 10% of reserved capacity + burst credits. With burst credits at 0 we're basically stuck.

maria (eng-support): Two quick hypotheses: 1) noisy neighbor (another tenant on same pool) caused sustained TPS so credits drained. 2) prewarm/autoscale thresholds were lowered in last config change so scaler waited too long to prewarm. I see a config commit yesterday that reduced prewarm_reserved=1 -> 0.

ajay (oncall): That config change would explain reduced immediate headroom, thanks. Can we repro locally for the admission logic? Maria, can you share a minimal load repro script we can run against a staging pool? We should also check if billing/auth overrides delayed credit refills.

maria (eng-support): Repro curl loop (staging) — ramp to 2k tps across 4 clients: ```for i in {1..2000}; do curl -s -X POST "https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":1}'; done``` Add concurrency via xargs -P 4. Watch admission logs.

simon (infra): I pulled allocation events — we had a quota error from cloud provider at 08:18: `RESOURCE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED: GPUs 2 exceeds project quota`. Support ticket with provider opened. That explains why autoscale didn't complete.

ajay (oncall): Short term mitigation options: 1) increase per-customer throttle for Venue to soften peak (apply quota config) 2) temporarily move some noise-causing tenants off this pool 3) manually bump reserved capacity if cloud quota allows in another account/region. Venue wants ETA for fix.

venue-sre: Customer prefers fastest fix. They asked for temporary throttle on noisy tenants if that is easiest.

maria (eng-support): I'll prepare a targeted throttle and a playbook: - identify top callers by API key (query logs) - patch admission policy to cap per-key TPS for 30m - monitor credits and revert. Patch snippet: ```admission.policy.per_key_tps_limit = 250``` Will push to canary pool first.

simon (infra): Also recommend restoring prewarm_reserved=1 for this pool as a config rollback to give immediate headroom next time. I can stage that and roll in 5m.

ajay (oncall): Action items: - Maria to run log query and apply per-key throttle (ETA 10m) - Simon to rollback prewarm config (ETA 5m) - Simon to follow up with cloud quota ticket and explore alternate region (ETA 2h) - Tess to update Venue with ETA and mitigation steps.

tess (support): I'll update Venue now: telling them we're applying short-term per-key throttles and a config rollback to restore prewarm headroom. Will ask if they can shift heavy batch jobs away for the next hour.

venue-sre: Thanks. Also note that billing shows BurstCreditRefill events delayed by ~30s during the spike — might be edge case where refill loop is backlogged under high load.

maria (eng-support): Noted. Add check: ensure refill worker has dedicated CPU quota and backpressure handling. I'll open an infra task.

ajay (oncall): If the throttle + prewarm rollback doesn't bring 429s down within 15m we escalate to emergency reserved bump and apply emergency routing.

simon (infra): Prewarm rollback deployed to pool-vn-14 at 08:30 UTC. Ops shows burst credits still 0 but permitted headroom increased to 4 GPUs worth (virtual) so admission allows short bursts. Monitoring now.

ops-bot: [resolve] alert DedicatedPool(pool-vn-14) admission_reject < 10 req/min for last 5m. Incident state: recovering.

tess (support): Customer update: Venue confirms 429s subsided after throttle and rollback. They're monitoring. Next steps: follow-up postmortem and runbook updates.

maria (eng-support): I'll create a short postmortem doc with root cause (quota blocked autoscale + prewarm removal) and three mitigations (per-key throttles, ensure refill worker priority, autoscale quota fallback).

ajay (oncall): Great. Closing thread once postmortem link posted. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
